old: Principal findings: population structure. Zone differentiation is very low, and after the sensitivity analysis this is the best-supported finding in the report. The largest pairwise FST is 0.00232 (SE 0.00053, 95% CI 0.00128-0.00336) between coastal and Guinea savanna, and one of six pairs - Guinea savanna versus the transitional zone (n = 25) - has a confidence interval spanning zero; the other five have strictly positive lower bounds. Varying the two thresholds that define the dataset leaves the maximum pairwise FST within 0.00204-0.00255 across all six scenarios, over sample sizes from 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and SNP counts from 3,275 to 10,876. Two directions within that range are worth recording: relaxing the Fws cut slightly raises FST (0.00232 to 0.00255 with no Fws filter at all), so polyclonal isolates were not masking differentiation, and tripling the SNP count at MAF >= 0.01 lowers it (0.00204), as expected if rarer variants are less differentiated between zones. Isolation by distance, by contrast, is not a robust result. At administrative-region level the test is significant at the published thresholds (Mantel r = 0.427, p = 0.025 with negative FST pairs floored to zero; r = 0.414, p = 0.041 without flooring the three negative pairs) and it is absent at zone level (r = 0.471, p = 0.122, significant in 0 of 4 leave-one-zone-out replicates, and with four populations admitting only 24 distinct label permutations). But across the six threshold scenarios the region-level test is significant in only two: the published thresholds and MAF >= 0.02 (r = 0.434, p = 0.047 censored, p = 0.050 uncensored, so that scenario is marginal in both directions). It fails at every relaxation of the Fws monoclonality cut (Fws >= 0.90, r = 0.318, p = 0.087; Fws >= 0.80, r = 0.256, p = 0.169; no Fws filter, r = 0.245, p = 0.179) and at MAF >= 0.01 (r = 0.432, p = 0.062). It is also significant in only four of seven leave-one-region-out replicates, collapsing when Upper East is dropped. The finding holds at the published thresholds and almost nowhere else, and is reported here as not robust - not as a supported result, and not as a weak but real distance effect. ADMIXTURE cross-validation error is minimised at K = 2 (0.83925) over K = 1 (0.84384), an improvement of 0.00459 on a near-flat curve. The K = 2 minor component is not uniform across zones (means 0.092 deciduous forest, 0.085 coastal savanna, 0.053 Guinea savanna, 0.042 transitional zone; Kruskal-Wallis H = 105.4, p = 1.1 x 10 to the -22). That is a real contrast - coastal and forest high, Guinea savanna and transitional low - concordant with the FST ranking but not a monotone latitudinal cline, and of negligible magnitude. TreeMix, now run with edge standard errors, supports exactly two migration edges (weights 0.152, p = 7.5 x 10 to the -4, and 0.805, p = 3.3 x 10 to the -16; variance explained 0.9969 at m = 2 against 0.8970 at m = 0); a third edge is indistinguishable from zero (p = 0.33).

old: [Calculated] Principal findings: drug-resistance markers. The previous version's resistance findings were affected by a defect in how markers were identified - the panel matched SnpEff protein-change strings, which can see neither a resistance allele that is itself the reference residue nor a residue that requires two nucleotide changes in one codon - and the panel has been rebuilt by codon reconstruction, which corrects it. Two findings follow directly from the rebuild. **pfdhps A437G, wholly absent from the previous panel, stands at 0.897* for G437 (n = 1,892; deciduous forest 0.964, coastal savanna 0.941, Guinea savanna 0.875, transitional zone 0.800; chi-square p = 1.2 x 10 to the -6); the official Pf8 methodology states that the 3D7 sequence translates as a G at 437 and that this is the mutant allele, so the resistance residue is the reference residue and no ALT annotation for it can exist. And the former "naming discrepancy" at pfcrt 75 was never a naming matter: N75E requires two SNPs in one codon (403621 A>G, annotated Asn75Asp; 403623 T>A, annotated Asn75Lys), and neither annotation names it. Haplotypes are now counted within isolates on complete cases. The pfdhfr IRN triple mutant is 0.771 (n = 1,876; 95% CI 0.751-0.789) - not the marginal range 0.786-0.908 previously quoted, and, as it must be, below its lowest component on the same complete-case set (51I = 0.788); NRN sits at 0.116 and the fully wild-type NCS at 0.091, so it is not a near-fixed single haplotype, and the quadruple IRNL is 0.000. pfcrt CVIET is 0.071 and is demonstrably a single unit: only CVMNK (0.929) and CVIET occur at codons 72-76, with nothing intermediate. pfdhps GE (437G + 540E) is 0.010. The pfdhfr marginals remain high and lowest in Guinea savanna (S108N 0.908 overall / 0.885 Guinea savanna; C59R 0.886 / 0.864; N51I 0.786 / 0.764; chi-square p = 9.4 x 10 to the -7, 4.8 x 10 to the -5 and 2.4 x 10 to the -4), with the transitional zone (n = 25) at or near the top of all three. The pfk13 panel was rebuilt from the WHO compendium v1.0 (December 2025) and covers all 14 validated markers (F446I, N458Y, C469Y, M476I, Y493H, G533S, R539T, I543T, P553L, R561H, P574L, C580Y, R622I, A675V) and all 6 candidates (E252Q, P441L, C469F, N537I, G538V, V568G); the old list was written from memory, misclassified P441L and C469F as validated when WHO classes them as candidate, and omitted P574L, G533S and R622I. All 23 pfk13 codons are fixed at the reference residue (codon 458 at 0.999), on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon of 1,900, across a 2009-2021 sampling period - a tested historical negative, not a statement about the present. old: [Interpreted] Conclusion. At the resolution these data permit, Ghanaian P. falciparum behaves as a largely panmictic unit. That is now the strongest claim this report carries, and the sensitivity analysis is the reason: the maximum pairwise FST stays within 0.00204-0.00255 across all six threshold scenarios, over 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so the headline result is insensitive to both of the cuts that define the dataset. The companion claim does not survive the same treatment. The region-level isolation-by-distance result is significant at the published thresholds and at MAF >= 0.02, but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, and this report therefore no longer asserts a distance effect, weak or otherwise. What remains of the spatial signal is a single south-to-north contrast, visible in the FST ranking and in the K = 2 minor component, with no robust evidence that genetic distance scales with geographic distance. That near-panmixia is a statement about neutral common-variant structure only: neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible, so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure, but marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the resistance panel in this analysis shows significant between-zone variation at p < 0.001 at pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1. That threshold is stated because it is a selection: on the four-zone chi-square as reported, several further loci are nominally significant at p < 0.05, among them pfcrt I356T (p = 1.6 x 10 to the -3), pfmdr2 I492V (p = 0.020) and pfmdr1 N86Y (p = 0.029). Low neutral FST therefore does not license an assumption that marker frequencies are spatially representative. The pfk13 result is a genuine tested negative - every one of the 23 codons, the complete WHO-validated set of 14 and all 6 candidates, fixed at the reference residue, codon 458 at 0.999, on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon - rather than an untested absence; it is also a statement about 2009-2021 and not about current parasite populations. The XtX set remains a ranked candidate list, of which 13 SNPs survive FDR 10% and two adjacent chromosome-11 sites - one of them the fifth-ranked SNP overall - are flagged lower confidence on ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff grounds. All zone-level results describe a compound variable in which ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing study cannot be separated; that is a property of the Pf8 metadata, not of the analysis.

old: [Interpreted] Questions 1, 3 and 4 are answerable at the resolution these data permit and are answered in Section 6. Question 1 is answered robustly: the low-differentiation reading survives both threshold relaxations, with max FST between 0.00204 and 0.00255 across the six scenarios. Question 2 is answered negatively. The distance effect it tests is significant at the published thresholds but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, so the honest answer is that these data do not establish isolation by distance; whether that is a statement about Ghanaian parasite demography or about the fragility of a Mantel test on 21 pairs from 7 coordinates cannot be settled here, and both readings are consistent with everything else in the report. Question 5 is answerable only in the weak sense of producing a ranked candidate list: with four populations and 3,916 SNPs the scan has limited power, 3.9 of the 19 SNPs above the quantile threshold are expected to be false positives, only 13 survive FDR 10%, and two - including the fifth-ranked SNP overall - carry ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signatures that put them at lower confidence. Question 6 is answered directly, by genotyping rather than by scan, which is why a reference-residue frequency of 1.000 at a pfk13 codon is now informative where a non-significant XtX value would not have been - subject to two limits that must travel with the number. It is fixation among called genotypes, 1,845 to 1,876 isolates per codon rather than all 1,900, and it describes isolates collected between 2009 and 2021. The corroborating MalariaGEN kelch13 status exists for only 36 of those isolates, because Pf8 treats any missing call across amino acids 349-726 as undetermined, so it is supporting rather than independent evidence.

[Observed] The codon panel bypasses the release filter as well as the numalt filter, and that was not previously disclosed. Stage 12 reconstructs codons from every variant record at a panel position, iterating over all ALT alleles without consulting FILTER_PASS. Bypassing numalt == 1 was the deliberate fix that recovered the panel; bypassing FILTER_PASS came with it and was never stated. An audit of all 171 panel positions resolves what it costs. Of the variant records at those positions, 29 fail the release filter, at 29 distinct positions. Among the 1,900 analysis isolates, six non-reference calls are sourced from those 29 records, at three positions, and all three are in pfk13 at WHO-validated marker codons: 1,724,975 (codon 675, A675V) with four carriers, 1,725,315 (codon 561, R561H) with one, and 1,725,339 (codon 553, P553L) with one. None of the six changes a reported residue, for two separable reasons. At codons 561 and 553 every alternative allele at the failing position is synonymous — the reference codons are CGT and CCG, and the ALTs give CGG, CGC, CGA and CCA, CCT, which still encode Arg and Pro — so the one homozygous call among the six, isolate SPT19969 at codon 561, correctly counts as Arg561 and the reported 1,864 of 1,864 is right. At codon 675 the alternative is non-synonymous but encodes Pro, not the validated Val, and all four carriers are heterozygous, so the mixed-call rule made the codon uncalled for them. No screened WHO resistance residue is produced by any filter-failing record, and the tested negative therefore stands. One consequence should still travel with the number: those four codon-675 carriers have well-supported minor alleles — 22% to 28% of 173 to 435 reads at GQ 99 — so codon 675's denominator of 1,845 is the lowest in the panel, and its exclusions are not random with respect to genotype.

[Observed] The single Asn458Asp call was confirmed at read level and is genuine. Because one call in 1,866 at a validated marker codon could as easily be an annotation or base-calling artefact as a real variant, the underlying data were retrieved. Codon 458 draws on Pf3D7_13_v3 positions 1,725,626, 1,725,625 and 1,725,624. The middle position carries no variant record. The last fails the release filter and has no non-reference carrier among the 1,900. The first, 1,725,626, passes the filter and is triallelic (REF T, ALT A and C, numalt = 2), which is why the numalt == 1 ingest mask excluded it from the genome-wide matrix. Isolate PF0106-C is homozygous for the second ALT, C, with allele depths of 0, 0 and 40 — forty of forty reads supporting that allele — at DP 40 and GQ 99, the maximum. On the minus strand C complements to G, turning the reference codon AAT into GAT, which is Asp. The call is unambiguous at the read level and the reconstruction is arithmetically correct. It is also not the validated allele: WHO validates N458Y, which requires AAT to TAT, a different substitution at the same base. So codon 458 is 0.9995 reference rather than fixed, the one alternative residue is Asp and not Tyr, and no WHO-screened artemisinin marker is observed.

new: [Interpreted] A two-edge graph is the model these data select, and m = 2 is reported as a descriptive model rather than as a count of historical migration events. This narrows a question the original manuscript left open, but it does not close it the way a count of historical events would be closed. The plateau rule applied to variance explained picks m = 2 within the identifiable range and m = 3 across the full sweep, and with no edge p-values there was no way to choose between them; the manuscript retained both. The edge p-values now favour m = 2 — but they do so as a conditional test inside a graph whose topology, root and edge count were all fixed before the test was run, and they do not agree with the variance-explained criterion applied over the full sweep, which reaches 0.9997 at m = 3 and so still prefers m = 3. The two criteria therefore disagree, and the disagreement is settled here on identifiability grounds, which is a modelling decision and not a measurement. What the statistics do support is narrower: the third edge is indistinguishable from zero on its own jackknife standard error, four populations support roughly two edges on parameter-counting grounds, and m = 2 is accordingly the graph reported as a descriptive model. It is not an estimate of how many admixture events occurred in the history of Ghanaian P. falciparum, and no uncertainty in topology, root placement or edge count is propagated into it. The earlier hedging between m = 2 and m = 3 is replaced by a stated model choice, not by a resolution.

[Calculated] One printed edge p-value is a floating-point artefact, and it is recorded here so that it is not carried forward as a measured quantity. At m = 3 the second edge is reported with jackknife mean 0.829575, standard error 0.0787911 and p < 2.22507 × 10⁻³⁰⁸. That p-value is not consistent with its own mean and standard error: z = 0.829575/0.0787911 = 10.53, whose one-sided normal tail is about 3.2 × 10⁻²⁶, and 2.2250738585072014 × 10⁻³⁰⁸ is exactly DBL_MIN, the smallest normal double-precision float. The figure is TreeMix’s underflow sentinel, not a computed tail probability. Recomputing all six edge p-values from the printed means and standard errors reproduces the other five to three significant figures — at m = 1, z = 7.84 gives 2.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ against the printed 2.22045 × 10⁻¹⁵; at m = 2, z = 3.18 gives 7.48 × 10⁻⁴ against 0.000747653 and z = 8.06 gives 3.80 × 10⁻¹⁶ against 3.33067 × 10⁻¹⁶; at m = 3, z = 3.09 gives 9.91 × 10⁻⁴ against 0.00099053 and z = 0.446 gives 0.328 against 0.327622. Two consequences follow. The reproduction confirms that the final run did compute jackknife standard errors, which an earlier script snapshot lacking the -se flag had put in doubt; and the anomalous value belongs to the rejected m = 3 model, while the two p-values the m = 2 choice rests on are both reproducible, so no reported result depends on it.

F~ST~, ADMIXTURE and TreeMix are three summaries of one genotype matrix: all three are computed from the same per-zone allele counts, and at this level of differentiation a four-population covariance matrix and the pairwise F~ST~ matrix are near-deterministic functions of each other. Only the ordinations use a different input — MalariaGEN's published Pf8 genotype-distance matrix — and they are now computed on the same 1,900 isolates as everything else, because stage 3 has been re-run on the analysis set (silhouette by zone −0.020; Table 8.2 row 21, Figure 8.1). The agreement between rows 1, 3 and 4 of Table 7.1 is therefore substantially arithmetic, not corroborative. What this revision adds is robustness rather than independence: the F~ST~ summary has been recomputed under six combinations of the two thresholds that define the dataset, and the maximum pairwise value moves only between 0.00204 and 0.00255 (row 5 of Table 7.1; Table 8.3). Those six scenarios are not independent lines either — they are the same pipeline on overlapping data — but they establish that the headline does not depend on the analyst's threshold choices, which is a different and more useful thing. The region-level Mantel test does not share that robustness, and it has to be given up. It is a fourth summary of the same matrix, computed from region-level F~ST~, so it was never independent of the others; and it is significant in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, so it cannot be cited as a converging line at all (Table 7.2, row 1). It was the one result here carrying a positive structure claim, and losing it is a real loss rather than a tidying-up. Described accurately, what remains is: three summaries of one 3,916-SNP genotype matrix (ADMIXTURE on 3,385 LD-pruned sites of it), plus three ordinations of an independently published distance matrix on the same 1,900 isolates, all pointing the same way, and insensitive to both thresholds that define the dataset. [Interpreted] It cannot establish that the retained panel is neutral, because no neutral mask was ever defined. The 3,916 SNPs are the sites that survived the FILTER_PASS, biallelic-SNP, missingness and minor-allele-frequency criteria, and not one of those is a neutrality criterion: no coding or non-coding partition, no synonymous/non-synonymous distinction, no gene-proximity exclusion and no recombination-rate weighting was applied at any stage. The panel therefore contains the resistance loci themselves — the XtX scan is run on this same panel and returns pfaat1 and PTP7 from it — so the set used to measure background differentiation also contains the sites under the strongest selection in the genome. That inclusion is very unlikely to be driving the differentiation result: 19 outliers among 3,916 sites cannot move a ratio-of-averages estimator away from 0.002, and the maximum FST is stable at 0.00204–0.00255 across six scenarios that change the panel composition substantially. The point is not that the number is wrong but that the word is unearned. Wherever “neutral” appears in this report it should be read as “genome-wide at the retained common variants”, never as “at sites shown to be free of selection”. Building a genuine neutral mask — excluding the known resistance loci, the antigenic and invasion gene families, and sites in high linkage with them, then recomputing differentiation on what remains — is a specified next step and is not done here.

[Calculated] The pooled minor-allele-frequency filter imposes an ascertainment floor set by the largest zone. Allele counts are pooled across all 1,900 isolates before the 5% cut is applied, and Guinea savanna contributes 1,334 of them — 70.2% of the sample — against 337 deciduous forest, 204 coastal savanna and 25 transitional. With the variant-missingness ceiling of 10%, a retained site carries at least 1,710 called haploid alleles. A variant private to the transitional zone therefore cannot exceed 25/1,710 = 1.46% and is excluded even if every one of those 25 isolates carries it; a variant at 40% frequency in coastal savanna reaches only 82/1,710 = 4.80% and is excluded as well. The 3,916-SNP panel is accordingly a panel of variants common enough to clear a threshold dominated by one zone, and every differentiation statistic computed on it — the pairwise FST, the three ordinations, the ADMIXTURE fit, the population graph and the Mantel test — inherits that restriction. This does not bias the FST estimates themselves, which are computed on the sites that were retained and are unaffected by the existence of sites that were not. It bounds their scope. “Negligible differentiation” is a statement about commonly shared variation; it is not evidence against zone-restricted or locally common variants, which this design cannot see at all. The maf001 and maf002 scenarios probe the floor only partly: they raise the panel to 10,876 and 6,852 SNPs and leave maximum FST at 0.00204 and 0.00217, but both still pool allele counts across zones, so they lower the floor rather than remove it. Removing it would require either frequency filtering within zones or a design in which the zones contribute comparable numbers of isolates.
